meta.source: Reserve Bank of India, DBIE (via the Data Bank)
meta.revisionPolicy: Each year passes through three stages: the budget estimate (February before the year), the revised estimate (February of the year) and the accounts (provisional in May after the year, audited later). The RBI's tables restate a year as it moves from one stage to the next; each stage is kept as its own series.
meta.coverage: Which states ran short of cash: days each state drew on the RBI's special drawing facility, ways and means advances and overdraft, and the average amount, every month since September 2017
meta.note: RBI Bulletin, Financial Accommodation Availed by State Governments under various Facilities (DBIE report 63). SDF is drawn against the state's reserve funds and Treasury bills held with the RBI; WMA is the RBI's advance for temporary cash mismatches; overdraft is anything beyond the WMA limit (the table's notes 1 to 3). Average amount is the total drawn divided by the days it was drawn (note 4). The table prints '-' for nil: read as zero. State counts are computed here.
